header.title: Frequently Asked Questions
header.desc: Everything you want to know about our services, treatments, and what to expect at Matikyan Dental Clinic.

general.q: How often should I visit the dentist?
general.a: We recommend a routine check-up and professional cleaning every 6 months. Patients with gum disease, frequent cavities, or orthodontic appliances may need visits more often.

general.q: What should I bring to my first appointment?
general.a: Please bring a photo ID, insurance information if applicable, recent dental X-rays if available, and a list of current medications.
We try to accommodate dental emergencies the same day. For planned treatment, booking ahead is the best way to secure your preferred time.

treatments.a: Yes. Professional whitening is safe when it is carried out after an appropriate dental assessment and with materials suited to your teeth and gums.

treatments.q: How long do dental implants last?
treatments.a: With proper care, implants can serve for many years. Long-term success depends on oral hygiene, bone support, bite control, and regular follow-up visits.
Traditional porcelain veneers usually require some enamel preparation, so they are generally considered irreversible. We explain all conservative and restorative options during consultation.

treatments.q: How painful is a root canal?
treatments.a: Modern root canal treatment is typically managed comfortably with effective anesthesia. Most patients describe it as far easier than they expected.

invisalign.q: Am I a candidate for Invisalign?
invisalign.a: Invisalign is often suitable for mild to moderate crowding, spacing, and selected bite issues. A clinical exam and digital assessment are the best way to confirm whether it fits your case.

invisalign.q: How long does Invisalign treatment take?
invisalign.a: Treatment time depends on complexity, but many cases fall between 6 and 24 months. Your plan is based on the exact movements required.

payment.a: Insurance and reimbursement conditions depend on your provider and treatment type. Our team can review the expected details with you before care begins.
For more complex treatment plans, available payment arrangements can be discussed with the clinic team in advance.

payment.q: What is the cost of a consultation?
payment.a: Consultation costs depend on what is included in the visit, such as imaging or specialist assessment. We explain this clearly before scheduling.

cta.title: Still Have Questions?
cta.desc: Our team is available to answer practical questions about visits, treatment planning, and next steps.

dentalCleaningCheckup.title: Dental Cleaning & Check-up
dentalCleaningCheckup.desc: Professional teeth cleaning removes tartar and plaque that regular brushing cannot reach. The visit also includes an oral exam, digital imaging review, and gum health assessment.
dentalCleaningCheckup.intro: Routine preventive visits help keep small issues from turning into complex treatment. At Matikyan Dental Clinic, a cleaning and check-up combines professional hygiene, a full exam, and practical guidance for daily care.
dentalCleaningCheckup.h2Title: What to expect during your visit
dentalCleaningCheckup.h2Description: Your appointment is designed to assess oral health, clean hard-to-reach buildup, and identify concerns early so treatment can stay conservative.
process: A review of your current symptoms, oral hygiene habits, and dental history.
Professional cleaning to remove tartar, plaque, and superficial staining.
Clinical examination of teeth, gums, bite, and existing dental work.
candidates: Patients due for routine preventive care.
Adults and teens who want a baseline oral health review.
Anyone noticing bleeding gums, staining, or sensitivity.

teethWhitening.title: Professional Teeth Whitening
teethWhitening.tagline: Up to 8 shades brighter in one visit
teethWhitening.desc: In-clinic whitening using a professional-grade gel and controlled light activation for visible, even brightening in a single appointment.
teethWhitening.intro: Professional whitening is one of the fastest ways to refresh a smile. Our treatment plan is built around your enamel condition, shade goals, and sensitivity history.
teethWhitening.h2Description: We evaluate the cause of discoloration first, then use a controlled in-office process to brighten teeth safely and evenly.
process: Shade assessment and suitability check before treatment starts.
Gum protection and controlled application of professional whitening gel.
Post-treatment review with maintenance advice for longer-lasting results.
candidates: Patients with staining from coffee, tea, wine, or smoking.
Adults seeking a non-invasive cosmetic refresh.
Patients who want brighter teeth before weddings or events.

veneers.title: Porcelain Veneers
veneers.desc: Ultra-thin porcelain shells crafted to improve color, shape, gaps, and chips while keeping the result balanced and natural-looking.
veneers.intro: Porcelain veneers can reshape the visible smile line with a highly controlled cosmetic result. Treatment is planned around facial balance, tooth proportion, and a natural finish.
veneers.h2Description: Veneers are commonly used to improve chipped edges, uneven spacing, stubborn discoloration, and shape irregularities in the front teeth.
process: Cosmetic consultation and smile planning to define the final look.
Preparation and impressions or digital records for laboratory fabrication.
Final fitting and bonding of custom porcelain veneers.
candidates: Patients with front teeth affected by chips, spacing, or uneven form.
Adults seeking a longer-term cosmetic solution than whitening alone.
Patients willing to invest in custom cosmetic treatment planning.

compositeBonding.title: Composite Bonding
compositeBonding.desc: Tooth-colored composite resin used to repair chips, close gaps, and refine tooth shape without extensive preparation.
compositeBonding.intro: Composite bonding is a conservative cosmetic option for patients who want visible improvement without a laboratory-made restoration. It works especially well for small defects and same-day smile refinement.
compositeBonding.h2Description: Bonding is often selected for modest cosmetic corrections where preserving natural tooth structure is a priority.
process: Shade selection and planning of the desired contour changes.
Layering and sculpting of tooth-colored composite resin.
Finishing and polishing to blend the restoration with surrounding teeth.
candidates: Minor chips, uneven edges, and narrow gaps.
Patients who want a more affordable cosmetic option than veneers.
Patients looking for same-day cosmetic enhancement.

dentalImplants.title: Dental Implants
dentalImplants.desc: Titanium implants support stable, natural-looking restorations and help preserve bone structure after tooth loss.
dentalImplants.intro: Dental implants replace missing teeth with a stable, long-term solution that supports both appearance and function. Planning focuses on bone support, bite stability, and the final prosthetic result.
dentalImplants.h2Description: Successful implant treatment depends on diagnostics, surgical planning, and restoration design, not just implant placement alone.
process: Consultation with imaging to evaluate bone levels and restoration goals.
Implant placement with healing time based on the clinical case.
Final crown or prosthetic restoration after integration is complete.
candidates: Patients missing one or more teeth.
Patients wanting a fixed alternative to removable solutions.
Cases where preserving adjacent healthy teeth is important.

sameDayCrowns.title: Same-Day Crowns (CEREC)
sameDayCrowns.desc: Digital scanning and in-clinic milling make it possible to place a ceramic crown in one visit for selected restorative cases.
sameDayCrowns.intro: Same-day crowns are designed for patients who need strength, fit, and efficiency without multiple restoration appointments. Digital design helps reduce delays while maintaining restorative precision.
sameDayCrowns.h2Description: Digital scanning and in-house fabrication allow the tooth to be prepared, designed, and restored in a single clinical session.
process: Preparation of the tooth and digital scanning instead of traditional impressions.
In-house design and milling of the crown based on the digital model.
Try-in, adjustment, and final placement during the same visit.
candidates: A crown after fracture, decay, or root canal treatment.
A faster restorative timeline with fewer appointments.
A metal-free ceramic restoration with digital precision.

rootCanalTreatment.title: Root Canal Treatment
rootCanalTreatment.desc: Modern endodontic treatment removes infection from inside the tooth and helps preserve your natural tooth comfortably.
rootCanalTreatment.intro: Root canal treatment is used to save a tooth affected by deep infection or inflammation. The goal is to remove the diseased pulp, seal the canals, and keep the natural tooth functional.
rootCanalTreatment.h2Title: When a root canal is recommended
rootCanalTreatment.h2Description: Treatment is commonly advised when pain, deep decay, trauma, or infection has affected the inner nerve space of the tooth.
process: Diagnosis and imaging to confirm the affected tooth and canal anatomy.
Cleaning and shaping of the root canals under local anesthesia.
Sealing of the canals and planning for final restoration if needed.
candidates: Persistent toothache, pressure pain, or prolonged sensitivity.
Deep decay or infection close to the tooth nerve.
Teeth that can be preserved instead of extracted.

invisalign.title: Invisalign Clear Aligners
invisalign.desc: Clear removable aligners designed with digital planning for discreet correction of crowding, spacing, and selected bite issues.
invisalign.intro: Invisalign offers a discreet orthodontic option for patients who want straighter teeth without fixed brackets. Treatment planning is guided by digital records and staged aligner movement.
invisalign.h2Description: Clear aligner therapy is designed to correct crowding, spacing, and selected bite concerns while fitting more easily into daily routines.
process: Digital scanning and orthodontic assessment of alignment goals.
A staged aligner sequence designed around the desired tooth movement.
Progress reviews and refinements during treatment when needed.
candidates: Adults and teens wanting a low-visibility orthodontic solution.
Mild to moderate crowding or spacing cases.
Patients able to wear aligners consistently each day.

ceramicBraces.title: Ceramic Braces
ceramicBraces.desc: Tooth-colored braces provide reliable control for more complex alignment and bite correction with a subtler appearance than metal braces.
ceramicBraces.intro: Ceramic braces combine the control of fixed orthodontics with a more discreet appearance than traditional metal brackets. They are often chosen when a case needs detailed tooth movement.
ceramicBraces.h2Description: Ceramic braces are useful for patients who need comprehensive orthodontic correction but prefer a subtler appearance during treatment.
process: Orthodontic assessment and treatment planning for alignment and bite goals.
Placement of ceramic brackets and regular adjustment visits.
Monitoring through active movement until the final result is reached.
candidates: Adults and teens needing fixed orthodontic treatment.
Patients with moderate to complex bite or alignment issues.
Cases where aligners may not offer enough control.

periodontalTreatment.title: Periodontal Treatment
periodontalTreatment.desc: Targeted care for gum inflammation, recession, and periodontal disease, from deep cleaning to specialist follow-up support.
periodontalTreatment.intro: Periodontal treatment addresses inflammation, gum recession, and bone loss caused by gum disease. Early intervention helps preserve both teeth and supporting structures.
periodontalTreatment.h2Description: Treatment depends on disease stage, pocket depth, and tissue response, with the goal of controlling infection and stabilizing long-term oral health.
process: Clinical periodontal assessment and charting of gum health.
Deep cleaning, scaling, or targeted periodontal therapy.
Maintenance planning to reduce recurrence and monitor healing.
candidates: Bleeding gums, persistent bad breath, or gum tenderness.
Diagnosed gum disease or deep periodontal pockets.
Recession or bone loss that needs specialist attention.

wisdomToothExtraction.title: Wisdom Tooth Extraction
wisdomToothExtraction.desc: Removal of impacted or problematic wisdom teeth with careful planning, comfort measures, and aftercare guidance.
wisdomToothExtraction.intro: Wisdom tooth extraction is recommended when third molars cause pain, crowding, inflammation, or repeated infection. Planning focuses on comfort, safety, and predictable healing.
wisdomToothExtraction.h2Description: Impacted, partially erupted, or poorly positioned wisdom teeth can affect adjacent teeth and gum health, making timely removal the better long-term option.
process: Examination and imaging to assess tooth position and complexity.
Removal under local anesthesia with sedation options if appropriate.
Aftercare instructions and recovery monitoring after the procedure.
candidates: Pain, swelling, repeated infection, or food trapping around wisdom teeth.
Impacted teeth affecting neighboring molars.
Orthodontic or preventive reasons based on clinical assessment.

pediatricDentistry.title: Pediatric Dentistry
pediatricDentistry.desc: Child-friendly preventive and restorative dental care designed to build healthy habits and confident early visits.
pediatricDentistry.intro: Pediatric dentistry focuses on prevention, healthy habits, and positive early dental experiences. Visits are structured to help children feel comfortable while giving parents clear guidance.
pediatricDentistry.h2Description: Regular pediatric dental care supports healthy development, early cavity prevention, and timely monitoring of bite and tooth eruption patterns.
process: A child-friendly exam adapted to age and comfort level.
Preventive care such as cleaning, fluoride, and sealant recommendations.
Guidance for parents on hygiene, diet, habits, and early orthodontic concerns.
candidates: Children from first visits through adolescence.
Families who want preventive monitoring and education.
Children who benefit from a gentler, confidence-building dental approach.
